title: fix(Configure): use props a unique source of truth
body:
With this PR I removed the fact that we can read `<Configure>` parameters from the search state, as it's not easy to handle if we also provide a way to change them directly from the props. 

The props passed through `Configure` will only be pushed to search state. If the parameters needs to be modified, then the props of `Configure` needs to be modified. It means that when reading from a url, then the configure parameters must be extracted and passed through the props. 

If three params where passed to the `Configure` at the first rendering, and then as the second one only two props are passed, then the third one will disappear from the `search state`.

One use case illustrating the issue: 

Initial: Configure props is `hitsPerPage=3`

Step1: pass new props to configure to be `hitsPerPage=1`

Now the `search state` has `hitsPerPage=1`. 

Step2: pass new props to configure to be `hitsPerPage=2`

If we look at the search state first, this will never be applied. 

-- 

One obvious use case to read from the `search state` would be when you are loading the page and read the state from the URL. So reading from the state when the component did mount should do the trick for this case, but for now we don't have the architecture for it. 

Before the PR, the way it could have worked was when unmounting systematically the `<Configure/>` widget before passing it new props. 

With the PR, the search state is never taken into account, and you need to pass the right props directly to the `<Configure/>` widget.

@mthuret Can you ensure we do have a full example doing an url synchronisation with Configure where we re-read state and apply props dynamically? I am not sure we do have that today while it's critical to users.

So I added a geo-search recipe to show how you can update search parameters and synchronize the URL. I also updated the search parameters guide. 

This geo search example is very basic and only feature:

* a regular search through the searchbox. 
* a map that when we click somewhere perform a new search. 

We still need to do #1860 because with this example:

* the search is not triggered when moving the map. (mostly because I didn't find a `dragEnd` event with the lib used at the moment). 
* No autocomplete.
